cta: What should we open up next? Tell us in the comments
title: How Does ASML's EUV Machine Print a Chip With Light?

facts.label: Wavelength of EUV light, in nanometres
Times every second a tin droplet is hit and turned into light-making plasma
Diameter of each molten tin droplet, in microns (about)
Speed the droplets leave the generator, in metres per second
Smallest feature a standard (0.33 NA) EUV machine prints, in nanometres
Smallest feature a High-NA (0.55 NA) EUV machine prints, in nanometres

beats.say: The chip in a modern phone holds billions of tiny switches, and its finest lines were printed with light made by blowing up drops of molten tin.

params.place: inside the light source of an EUV machine: falling drops of molten tin flash into violet plasma in the dark

moments.what: drops of molten tin already falling through the dark chamber
a drop bursts into a violet-white flash
the flash swells into a glowing ball of plasma
the big curved mirror behind it lights up
another drop flashes
drop after drop flashes in a fast rhythm
a counter on the chamber wall starts counting

beats.say: The machine that does it, built by ASML, is about the size of a bus, and it blasts {fact2} drops of tin every second. So how does exploding metal end up as a chip?

params.place: a yellow-lit chip factory bay: the EUV machine as a long white enclosure, a bus outline beside it for size

moments.what: the long white machine hums in the yellow light, its status lights blinking
the outline of a city bus draws itself beside the machine
the screen on the machine counts up the drops
violet light pulses in its window
a question mark lights over the machine
a side panel slides open, violet light spilling out
a silicon wafer glides out of the loading port

beats.say: Follow the light through it. Tin becomes light, mirrors carry it, a mask gives it a pattern, and a silicon wafer takes the print.

params.place: the machine cut open, its light path from the tin source to the wafer stage laid out

moments.what: the machine's walls turn to glass, every stop dark inside
a dotted light path draws through the machine
the tin source at the start glows violet
the chain of mirrors lights one by one
the mask at the top lights
a pattern flickers onto the mask
the wafer at the bottom lights
a pulse of light runs the whole path

beats.say: Along the way, we'll see why no lens can do this job, how the newest machine prints even finer, and how one print becomes a working switch.

params.place: the same cutaway, its stops turning into chapter signs

moments.what: the lit path from the last shot, the camera drifting along it
a glass lens appears on the path and is crossed out
the mirrors brighten in its place
the wafer's lines sharpen and narrow
a tiny switch rises out of the wafer
current flickers through it
every stop glows at once

beats.say: It starts with tin, a soft silvery metal, heated until it melts and flows like water.

params.place: the droplet generator: a small heated tin reservoir glowing orange behind a steel nozzle

moments.what: the reservoir of tin sits on its heater, the nozzle below it
a bar of silvery tin drops into the reservoir
the heater glows orange, the tin bar softening
the tin slumps into a shining liquid
liquid tin runs down toward the nozzle

beats.say: A nozzle squeezes it out as a stream of tiny drops, each about {fact3} microns across, narrower than a human hair.

params.place: the nozzle tip in close-up, a line of shining tin drops leaving it

moments.what: the nozzle holds a bead of tin at its tip
the nozzle pulses and the bead breaks off
a long line of drops runs out of the nozzle
a ring and a scale bar lock round one drop
a human hair slides in beside the drop, much thicker

beats.say: Each one leaves the nozzle at about {fact4} metres a second, and they never stop coming.

params.place: the stream of drops rushing away from the nozzle in streaks

moments.what: drops stream out of the nozzle
the drops stretch into speed streaks
a speed tag rides along beside one drop
the stream doubles in density
the nozzle pulses again

beats.say: That's faster than a car on a motorway, and the nozzle aims every one of them at the same tiny spot.

params.place: the stream of drops racing toward the target spot

moments.what: drops race out of the nozzle
they stretch into streaks
a car outline races beside the stream, falling behind
the nozzle pulses
a ring marks the target spot
a drop crosses it exactly

beats.say: How many? {fact2} drops every second, falling one after another through the very same spot.

params.place: the chamber wall beside the stream, a counter screen bolted to it

moments.what: the stream falls past the screen
the counter screen counts up to the rate
the stream thickens
a ring marks the one spot where every drop passes
the spot blinks with each passing drop

beats.say: Why so many? Because every drop will become one short flash of light, and the machine needs a nonstop stream of flashes.

params.place: the target spot, the drops about to be lit

moments.what: the target spot glows faintly
drops keep falling through it
one drop flashes violet as it crosses
the next flashes too
the whole stream is visible
flash after flash in a steady rhythm

beats.say: And it all happens in a vacuum. This kind of light is swallowed by almost everything, even the air.

params.place: the sealed chamber, pumps drawing the air out

moments.what: specks of air drift through the chamber
the pump starts and the specks stream out
a violet ray leaves the spot
where air specks remain, the ray fades to nothing
the last specks are pumped out and the chamber is clear

beats.say: But a drop of tin doesn't glow on its own. So what turns it into light?

params.place: the empty target spot, a drop falling into it unlit

moments.what: drops fall through the spot, dull and silver
one drop is stopped in close-up, grey and dark
a question mark rises beside it
a window in the chamber wall lights red
a thin red line reaches toward the spot

beats.say: A laser. As each drop falls, a first, weaker pulse hits it and squashes it flat, like a tiny pancake.

params.place: the light source chamber: a laser window on one side, the target spot in the middle, the big curved mirror behind

moments.what: drops fall through the chamber
the laser window glows
time slows on one falling drop
a thin red pulse hits the drop
the drop squashes into a flat disc
the disc spreads into a wide, thin pancake

beats.say: Why flatten it? A wide, flat target catches far more of the next pulse, the big one.

params.place: the same chamber, the tin pancake hanging in the dark

moments.what: the pancake drifts in slow motion
a round drop appears beside it, much smaller
a target ring circles the pancake
a wide beam front washes over the pancake
the laser window charges up
a thick beam gathers in the window

beats.say: That main pulse is far more powerful, and it hits the pancake so hard that the tin becomes plasma, a gas so hot its atoms lose some of their electrons.

params.place: the target spot at the instant of the main pulse

moments.what: the pancake waits at the spot
the window blazes
a thick beam slams into the pancake
a white flash fills the chamber
a ball of glowing violet plasma swells
rings of heat ripple out from it
sparks fly out of the ball

beats.say: And that plasma glows. Not with light you could see, but with extreme ultraviolet light, at a wavelength of {fact1} nanometres.

params.place: the glowing plasma ball, waves of light leaving it

moments.what: the plasma ball glows
violet rays spread out of it
the rays fade to a faint shimmer
tight wave rings run out from the ball
the curved mirror behind catches them
one wave is drawn out on a ruler beside the ball

beats.say: What does that mean? The light our eyes see has waves many times longer. A shorter wave draws a finer line, like a sharp pencil next to a thick marker.

params.place: beside the plasma, two waves on a ruler and two lines drawn under them

moments.what: the short violet wave on its ruler
a long red-to-green visible wave draws above it
the visible wave stretches far past the violet one
the violet wave tightens
under each wave a line is drawn: a fat one and a thin one
a sharp pencil tip draws the thin line
a thick marker smears the fat one

beats.say: Then it all repeats. Drop, flatten, flash, {fact2} times a second.

params.place: the chamber in a steady rhythm of flashes

moments.what: the plasma fades
the next drop falls in
it slows at the spot
the first pulse flattens it
the main pulse turns it to plasma
the wall counter races

beats.say: Behind every flash, a big curved mirror gathers the light and focuses it to one bright point at the far end of the chamber.

params.place: the collector mirror, a wide bowl behind the plasma, its light converging

moments.what: a flash glows in front of the bowl
the bowl mirror lights from inside
a cone of light gathers off the mirror
the cone narrows toward one point
the point blazes at the end of the chamber
light streams out through the exit

beats.say: Why tin, of all things? Tin plasma happens to glow brightly at just this wavelength, so more of each flash is light the machine can use.

params.place: the plasma ball in close-up, its glow measured

moments.what: the plasma ball glows
the next drops fall in
one bursts into plasma
violet rays pour off it
the short wave writes on beside it
another flash
the mirror behind takes the light

beats.say: So far: a drop, a flash, and light at {fact1} nanometres. Now it has to cross the machine, and this is where ordinary optics fail.

params.place: the cutaway machine, only the tin source lit

moments.what: the tin source glows
a drop falls in the source
it flashes
the light path ahead lights faintly
a glass lens slides onto the path
the light hits the lens and dies

beats.say: Why not a lens? A camera or a microscope bends light through glass. Try that here, and the glass simply swallows it.

params.place: a dark vacuum tunnel: a glass lens on a stand, a violet beam heading into it

moments.what: a violet beam runs down the tunnel
a glass lens rises onto the beam's path
a camera lens and a microscope lens ghost in beside it
a visible beam bends cleanly through the glass
the violet beam reaches the glass
it dies inside the glass, which warms orange

beats.say: So the light's path has no lenses at all. The machine steers it with mirrors instead.

params.place: the tunnel opening out onto a chain of mirrors

moments.what: a chain of mirrors rises along the tunnel
a violet beam enters the tunnel
it reaches the first mirror
the beam bounces from mirror to mirror
each mirror flashes as the beam lands

beats.say: Not ordinary mirrors, though. Each one is made of many very thin layers, two materials stacked one on top of the other.

params.place: one mirror cut open in close-up, its stack of layers showing

moments.what: the beam lands on one mirror
a wedge of the mirror lifts away
under its face, a stack of thin layers
the layers fan apart
alternate layers light in two colours
they settle back into one stack

beats.say: Each layer reflects back a little of the light, and all those small reflections line up into one strong bounce.

params.place: the layer stack, a beam coming down onto it

moments.what: the stack under its mirror face
a violet beam comes down into the stack
a faint reflection leaves every layer
the faint reflections line up side by side
they merge into one bright beam
the mirror flashes

beats.say: Why does that matter? Even the best mirror loses part of the light on every bounce, and the light bounces many times on its way down.

params.place: the mirror chain from the side, the beam dimming at each mirror

moments.what: the beam runs the chain
the first mirror shines
a glow bar beside it drops a step
each mirror the beam leaves dimmer
a row of glow bars steps down along the chain
the beam at the end is thin and faint

beats.say: It is the reason the source must be so bright, and why these mirrors are polished to some of the smoothest surfaces ever made.

params.place: a single mirror under a sweep of light

moments.what: the faint beam at the end of the chain
the beam brightens all along the chain
the end of the chain glows strong
one mirror fills the frame
a sweep of light glides across its face
the reflection on it is perfectly sharp

beats.say: So the light arrives clean and bright. But it carries no picture yet. Where does the pattern of a chip come from?

params.place: the end of the mirror chain, a plain bright beam heading up

moments.what: a bright beam leaves the last mirror
it lands clean
its spot of light is blank, no pattern in it
a question mark rises over the spot
the beam turns upward, out of the tunnel

beats.say: From the mask: a plate carrying the pattern of one layer of the chip, like a stencil.

params.place: the mask stage at the top of the machine: a square plate held face down, its pattern glinting

moments.what: the mask glides into its stage
it turns so its face shows
the chip's pattern draws on across its face
one layer's lines glow
a stencil and paint ghost in beside it

beats.say: And even the mask is a mirror. The light bounces off its pattern instead of shining through it.

params.place: the mask face down, a beam coming up to it

moments.what: the mask over the dark stage
a beam rises at an angle to the mask
the mask's face shines like a mirror
the beam bounces off and heads down
no light comes through the back of the plate

beats.say: Dark parts of it swallow the light, bright parts bounce it back, so the bounce carries the shape of the pattern.

params.place: the mask's face in close-up, light landing on its lines

moments.what: light on the mask
the dark lines stay black
the gaps between them shine
the bounced light leaves
the pattern is now printed into the beam itself
the patterned beam heads down

beats.say: That's also why the mask must stay perfectly clean. A single speck of dust on it would be printed onto every chip, again and again.

params.place: the mask face in close-up, one speck drifting toward it

moments.what: the mask under its light
its face gleams
a speck of dust drifts toward it
it lands on the pattern
the patterned light heads down
the speck's shadow lands on the wafer print
and on the next print, and the next

beats.say: And each of the chip's finest layers gets its own mask. Swap the mask, and the same machine prints a different layer.

params.place: the mask stage, one plate sliding out and another sliding in

moments.what: the mask in its stage
its lines glow
a rack of other masks lights beside the stage
the mask slides out and another slides in
the new pattern draws on
its different lines shine

beats.say: Then more mirrors shrink that picture down and aim it at the wafer below, far smaller than the mask itself.

params.place: the patterned beam dropping through mirrors toward the wafer

moments.what: the patterned beam heads down
a second set of mirrors lights below
the pattern shrinks as it passes them
the beam narrows onto one spot
the wafer's surface glows where it lands
the big pattern on the mask and the tiny print below light together

beats.say: Drawing the mask bigger than the print it makes keeps its pattern easier to make accurately.

params.place: the big mask above and its small print below, lit together

moments.what: the beam lands below
the mask's pattern redraws
outlines mark the big mask and the small print
the print glows
the mask's lines shine
its gaps light evenly

beats.say: And what is all that light printing onto?

params.place: the small bright print landing below

moments.what: the beam lands on the wafer
a question mark lights beside the spot
the wafer's surface glints
the camera dives at the spot

beats.say: A wafer: a thin, polished disc of silicon, coated with a film called a resist, which changes wherever the light lands.

params.place: the wafer stage: a shining silicon disc on a black chuck

moments.what: the silicon disc rests on its chuck
a highlight sweeps across it
the disc tilts toward us
a thin amber film spreads over it
a small square of the film changes colour under the light
the changed square glows

beats.say: It sits on a stage that races back and forth under the light, printing the pattern again and again, chip after chip, across the whole disc.

params.place: the wafer stage in motion under the slit of light

moments.what: a thin slit of light hangs over the wafer
the stage under the wafer lights its rails
the wafer slides fast under the slit
one square after another fills with the pattern
row after row of squares fill
the whole disc is covered in squares

beats.say: When one chip is done, the stage jumps to the next spot, and the next sweep begins, until every spot on the disc is printed.

params.place: the wafer stage stepping from square to square

moments.what: the slit over a finished square
the square glows done
the stage jumps over
the next square starts to fill
the slit brightens again
squares fill across the disc

beats.say: Above it, the mask moves too, in perfect step, so every line lands exactly where it should.

params.place: the mask overhead and the wafer below, gliding together

moments.what: the wafer slides under the slit
the mask above lights, sliding the other way
glowing links tie the two motions together
close on one square, a line lands
a crosshair locks on it

beats.say: How does the light print a whole chip at once? It doesn't. A thin slit of light sweeps across each one, like a scanner copying a page.

params.place: one chip-sized square in close-up, the slit sweeping over it

moments.what: the slit over the wafer
the whole square flashes, then fades: not like that
the square goes dark
a thin bar of light appears at its edge
it sweeps across, leaving the pattern behind
a page scanner's light bar ghosts in beside it
it copies a page the same way

beats.say: When the disc is done, it holds rows of identical chips, every one a copy of the same layer.

params.place: the finished wafer, its squares in rows

moments.what: the printed wafer
it tilts up to us
rows of squares light in order
each one glints the same
two squares light side by side, the same
light sweeps the whole disc

beats.say: And the finest lines a standard EUV machine prints are about {fact5} nanometres wide.

params.place: one square magnified to its finest lines

moments.what: a square in close-up
the camera dives into its lines
thin parallel lines fill the frame
a measuring bar spans one line
the width is written on the bar

beats.say: So far: tin becomes light, mirrors carry it, the mask shapes it, and the wafer takes the print. And the newest machine goes further.

params.place: the whole cutaway machine, every stop lit in turn

moments.what: the light path through the cutaway
the tin source flashes
the mirrors light
the mask lights
the wafer lights
a pulse runs the whole path
the lines on the wafer sharpen further

beats.say: It's called High-NA. Its mirrors are much bigger, and they catch the light at wider angles.

params.place: two optics benches side by side on a dark floor: a standard mirror on the left, a far bigger High-NA mirror on the right

moments.what: two mirrors on their benches
a sign lights over the right bench
the right mirror grows much larger
a cone of light comes off each mirror
the right cone opens far wider
arcs mark the two angles

beats.say: Why does a wider angle help? Light arriving from more directions can be focused to a tighter point, and a tighter point draws a finer line.

params.place: the two light cones meeting their focus points

moments.what: two cones of light
the angle arcs light
rays pour in from every side of the wide cone
each cone ends in a bright spot
the right spot shrinks far smaller
each spot draws a line: the right one thinner

beats.say: The result: lines about {fact6} nanometres wide, where the standard machine draws {fact5}.

params.place: the two printed lines side by side under measuring bars

moments.what: two lines drawn side by side
measuring bars drop over both
the right line's width writes on
the right line flashes
the left line's width writes on

beats.say: That's lines about {finer_ratio} finer, so more switches fit on the same patch of silicon.

params.place: a square patch of silicon, switches packing into it

moments.what: the two lines
a tag shows how much finer
two equal patches of silicon light below the lines
tiny switches pack into each: the right patch holds more
the switches glint

beats.say: Yet one pass under this light never makes a chip. A single pass prints just one layer, and a chip needs dozens of them.

params.place: one thin glowing layer lifting off the patch, an empty stack frame above it

moments.what: the patch of switches
one thin layer of it lifts and glows
the rest of the patch goes dark
the single layer hangs alone
a tall frame of empty layers rises above it

beats.say: What happens after the print? The wafer leaves the machine, and the resist is washed away where the light changed it, leaving a stencil.

params.place: a slice through the wafer's surface in close-up: silicon, then the resist film on top

moments.what: the slice of wafer, resist on top
stripes of the resist are the exposed ones
the block slides out of the machine's light
a rinse flows over the top
the exposed stripes wash away
the remaining resist stands as a stencil

beats.say: Then the gaps in that stencil are etched into the surface, or filled with metal.

params.place: the stencil on the surface, trenches cutting down through its gaps

moments.what: the stencil on top
its gaps glow
trenches cut down through the gaps
the trenches deepen into the surface
copper pours into the trenches
the metal shines

beats.say: The leftover resist is stripped off, a fresh layer goes on top, and the wafer goes back for the next print.

params.place: the surface cleaned, a new film spreading over it

moments.what: the filled trenches
the leftover resist lifts away
a fresh layer spreads over the top
new resist coats it
the block slides back toward the light
the next stripes are lit

beats.say: Print, wash, etch, fill: the same loop runs again for every layer, each one lined up exactly on the one below.

params.place: the slice of wafer cycling through the steps

moments.what: the stencil on top
stripes light under the print
a rinse sweeps over
trenches cut down
copper fills them
the copper shines
a crosshair lines the next layer up on this one

beats.say: At the very bottom, the first layers build the switches themselves: transistors, each a tiny gate that lets current through or blocks it.

params.place: the bottom of the chip's layer stack: rows of transistors on the silicon

moments.what: rows of transistors on the silicon
the lowest layers light
the transistors' fins rise
one gate glows pink
current flows through under it
the gate dims and the current stops

beats.say: What joins them up? Above them, layer after layer of copper wiring connects billions of those switches together.

params.place: the layer stack rising: copper wiring layers above the transistors

moments.what: the transistors
a question mark rises over them
a first layer of copper wiring lands on top
layer after layer of wiring stacks up
signals race along the wires
the whole stack stands tall

beats.say: And not every layer needs EUV. The bigger, coarser layers go to older machines that use longer-wave light, which costs less.

params.place: the layer tower, its upper layers changing colour

moments.what: the layer tower
the finest bottom layers glow violet
the upper, wider layers light amber
a wider, warmer beam lights the upper layers
longer waves ripple down that beam
the tower settles in two colours

beats.say: Only the finest layers, the ones packed tightest, take the trip through the tin and the mirrors.

params.place: the violet bottom layers in close-up

moments.what: the two-colour tower
the violet layers flare
their lines pack tight
a violet beam drops down onto them
a small flash at the beam's top
mirror glints along the beam

beats.say: After weeks of this, the finished wafer is sliced into separate chips.

params.place: the finished wafer on the stage, a saw line running across it

moments.what: the patterned wafer
light sweeps it
its chips glint in rows
saw lines run across it in a grid
one chip lifts free

beats.say: One of them is packaged, tested, and soldered onto the board inside a phone like yours.

params.place: the inside of a phone: its board, the chip dropping onto it

moments.what: a bare chip floats over a board
it is sealed into a package
test probes touch it and it lights green
it drops onto the board, solder glinting
the phone closes up around the board

beats.say: So follow that chip back one last time. Its switches were printed by light, the light was steered by mirrors, and the mirrors were lit by a flash.

params.place: the cutaway machine once more, the path lit backwards from the wafer to the source

moments.what: the cutaway machine
the wafer lights
a tiny switch rises from it
the light lights up the mask
the mirrors light
the path glows back toward the start
the tin source flashes

beats.say: The most advanced chips in phones, laptops and data centres all depend on a machine like this one.

params.place: the factory bay again, a row of EUV machines down the hall

moments.what: the machine hums in the yellow light
more machines light down the hall
a phone glows on the port
a laptop lights beside it
server racks glow at the far end
violet light pulses in every window

beats.say: A flash from one drop of tin, flattened, then blasted by a laser, one of {fact2} every second.

params.place: the light source chamber, one drop in slow motion

moments.what: drops falling
one slows at the spot
the first pulse flattens it
the main pulse strikes
the plasma blooms
the wall counter races

beats.say: All so the phone in your hand can carry billions of switches on a chip smaller than a fingernail.

params.place: the phone in a hand, opening into its board and the glowing chip, a fingertip beside it

moments.what: the phone glows in the hand
it opens up in layers
the chip in the board lights
its surface twinkles with switches
the chip lifts toward us
a fingertip comes in beside it, bigger than the chip

beats.say: What should we open up next? Tell us. Somewhere right now, another drop of tin is about to become light.

params.place: the light source chamber, as at the start, a drop falling toward the spot

moments.what: the chamber glows
drops fall again
the wall counter counts
one drop slows
the first pulse flattens it
it bursts into light

params.cta: What should we open up next?

references.what: the EUV machine in 3D, its insides lit purple, a loupe on the light
the real machine with its panels off, the inside showing
the High-NA machine opened up behind a presenter

thumbnails.pattern: one silicon wafer big in the frame, its grid of chips lit, a short verdict

references.what: a wafer filling the frame, its chips lit in colours
the chip itself as the hero on a plain ground, a few words
violet light striking the wafer inside the machine

made from sand: the raw material against the finished wafer
two chips side by side, before and after
